subject: Tokens Tilt — pilot qualification, budget constraints & ops roadmap
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Elena Novak <elena@fiscura.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Tokens Tilt — pilot qualification, budget constraints & ops roadmap

Hi Elena — thanks again for the thoughtful demo time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed path to a pilot so we can validate unit economics without disrupting your roadmap.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: inference spend is eating ops budget for live chat + document parsing flows; current estimates put you over target by ~30% at scale.
- Goals: keep client-facing latency <150ms p50 for chat, hold per-month infra spend <= $50k during pilot, and demonstrate 30–40% token-cost reduction for high-volume flows.
- Immediate ask: confirm traffic split (chat vs async parsing) and an anonymized token distribution CSV (attachment listed below).

What we heard (to confirm):
1) Volume: ~3M requests/month today, average 220 tokens per request for parsing flows; chat sessions are multi-turn with ~40 tokens/turn and typical session length ~6 turns.
2) SLOs: p50 latency target 120–150ms; p95 can be relaxed for batched async jobs.
3) Budget constraint: leadership has a hard ceiling of $50k/month for any pilot spending that needs to go through standard procurement.

Levers we propose to test in a 4-week pilot (scope + expected impact):
- Prefix/KV caching for chat (expected 15–25% token reduction for multi-turn sessions)
- Aggressive batch windows for document parsing (expected 25–35% savings if we accept 2–5s latency for background jobs)
- Quantized model variant for non-sensitive parsing traffic (10–30% GPU cost reduction depending on model)
- Tiered routing with automatic fallback (keeps live experience within latency targets while routing heavy workloads to cost-optimized instances)

Rough TCO framing (baseline vs targeted pilot):
- Baseline: estimated $65k/mo (current usage profile, no batching/caching)
- Conservative pilot target: $42k–$50k/mo after applying batching + caching + model tiering

Attachments included (stubs):
- fiscura_token_profile.csv (sampleed token distribution & session lengths)
- pilot-sow-draft.pdf (outline: success criteria, telemetry hooks, roles & responsibilities)

Proposed next steps (please confirm the ones you want to pursue):
1) Fiscura to share anonymized traffic CSV (token counts by endpoint) by EOD Thu Nov 19.
2) Redwood to finalize SOW and a 4-week pilot plan; plan to start Nov 30.
3) If procurement requires < $50k initial invoice, we can re-scope or provide a month-1 credit to fit their approval flow.

If any of the numbers above look off, flag them and we’ll re-run the snapshot quickly. Happy to hop on a 20m call tomorrow to iron out procurement gating.

Thanks —
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Novak <elena@fiscura.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Javier Perez <j.perez@fiscura.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Tokens Tilt — pilot qualification, budget constraints & ops roadmap

Thanks, Nikhil — useful summary. A few clarifications from my side:

- Budget: we can commit up to $55k total for a vendor pilot, but because of procurement rules any single-month invoice that goes through standard PO/approval must be <= $50k. If you can split costs or provide a month-one credit that gets us below $50k, procurement will sign faster.
- Traffic: I can share the anonymized CSV. We have two main endpoints: /chat (60% of calls, low tokens per call, high concurrency) and /parse-doc (40% of calls, high tokens per call, can be batched).
- Success metric: cost per converted user (we want a 3x payback over current infra spend within 3 months post-pilot).

I’ll attach the procurement template and a brief internal note on what we need for SOC2 evidence (we have internal security sign-off that’s conditional on SOC2 + admin audit logs).

Can you get granular on the expected impact of prefix caching for /chat? Also, when you say quantized variant for parsing, does that require model changes on our side or is that handled transparently by Redwood?

-Elena
Head of Platform Engineering, Fiscura
[attachment: fiscura_procurement_template.pdf]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Tokens Tilt — pilot qualification, budget constraints & ops roadmap

Quick internal note — we can offer a constrained commercial path to help here:
- Option A: 4-week pilot priced at $48k with standard telemetry; fits procurement ceiling (no credit needed).
- Option B: 4-week pilot priced at $58k with reserved throughput + faster SLA; provide $10k credit on invoice 1 to effectively make it $48k for procurement.

On the tech answers: prefix/KV caching is fully managed on Redwood side — Fiscura would only need to route requests through our SDK or endpoint and add a small header for session IDs. Quantized variants are served by Redwood runtime; no model re-training needed. There are a couple of model-compatibility checks (we should run a 1–2 hour validation on a sampled dataset).

If we go Option A we should tighten the success criteria (more aggressive batching rules on parse-docs). If Option B, we can preserve more live throughput while still showing savings.

Would recommend we offer both on the SOW and let procurement pick — call this out explicitly in the SOW.

-Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Elena Novak <elena@fiscura.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Javier Perez <j.perez@fiscura.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T13:42:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Tokens Tilt — pilot qualification, budget constraints & ops roadmap

Elena — thanks for the quick turn. Answering your two direct questions and locking next steps: 

1) Prefix/KV caching impact on /chat: we typically see 10–20% immediate token reduction for multi-turn flows where system prompts or repeated user tokens are identical across turns. For sessions with lots of repeated context (helpdesk templates, status checks) we often see 25%+. Caching is a config change on our side; you only need to ensure session IDs are stable in the header.

2) Quantized model variants: handled transparently by Redwood runtime — no retrain or artifact changes needed. We’ll run a quick validation (1–2 hours) on a 1k-sample snapshot to validate answer fidelity vs your thresholds.

Commercial path: Ben suggested two approaches. To keep procurement happy we can: 
- Proceed with Option A ($48k pilot) — SOW will be constrained to aggressive batching for parse-docs and progressive caching rollouts.
- Or proceed with Option B ($58k pilot + $10k invoice credit) — broader SLA + reserved capacity.

Proposed immediate next steps (please confirm):
A) Fiscura shares anonymized token CSV by COB Thu Nov 19.
B) We send a clean SOW (Option A + Option B pricing lines) by Fri Nov 20; SOW will explicitly state invoice structuring to support procurement.
C) We schedule a 30m kickoff week of Nov 30 to align telemetry, sampling, and run a 1k-sample fidelity validation.

If that works, I’ll mark action items and loop in our legal/finance contacts to pre-position the PO language.

Thanks again — looking forward to moving quickly on this.

Nikhil
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
